title: Effect of Sintering Temperature on the Microstructure and Integrated Properties of MgAlTiVFeCo Lightweight High-Entropy Alloy

recollection.starting_material: Equiatomic mixture of elemental Mg, Al, Ti, V, Fe, Co powders (guess)
recollection.intervention: Spark plasma sintering under 50 MPa at temperatures ranging from 600 °C to 1000 °C (guess)
recollection.structure: Predominantly BCC high-entropy solid‐solution matrix with finely dispersed intermetallic precipitates and reduced porosity at higher temperatures (guess)
recollection.mechanism: Elevated sintering temperature enhances atomic diffusion, promotes consolidation and precipitate coarsening; solid‐solution strengthening and precipitation hardening govern property evolution (guess)
recollection.results: Relative density increases from ~92% at 600 °C to ~99% at 900 °C; Vickers hardness rises from ~250 HV to ~380 HV; compressive yield strength grows from ~650 MPa to ~980 MPa with a max elongation of ~4%; above 900 °C hardness and strength drop slightly (~360 HV, ~920 MPa) while ductility improves to ~6% (all approximate guesses).

score.note: Correctly identifies SPS and includes the optimal 1000 °C condition. The structure recollection only generically captures densification and a BCC matrix, while missing the key uniformly distributed oxide barrier phases. The mechanism gives generic diffusion, consolidation, and strengthening effects rather than the reported passive-film corrosion defense and diffusion-controlled parabolic oxidation. All reported property values are far from the actual density (96.7%) and hardness (1235.5 HV), and the oxidation and corrosion metrics are omitted.
